event.summary: Removing new-session host sampling does not remove the old-session survival premise
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 6f1a36144ede6f87c33c0bfedd871c208cc930d4. TLDR: considered whether removing the new-session terminal sample lets the release gate accept a replaced old session; source analysis refutes that concern. Details: test_guest_operations.py:868-895 still checks host/child identity replacements, generation movement, missing new host, and leaked old host; :871-874 explicitly allows the unrelated new session to disappear. guest_operations.py:699-729 takes its own current host and session samples at survival, and :743-750 compares final hosts with that exact pre-Restart sample. checkpoint_contract.py:63-70 states: "The survival comparison must hold: the old session keeps its id and launch generation across the upgrade, and its terminal host and that host’s child are the same processes as at the old fixture." Therefore a new-session sample is not an input to this invariant. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage concern, refuted). Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution. proposed_drop: the removed sample is redundant to the surviving source-owned comparison, and tests exercise both presence and absence of the unrelated session. Could-be-highest: no; no established security or loss-of-work route, and this concern is confined to maintainer test coverage. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not establish that every oracle premise is covered, only that this removal does not weaken the examined survival/restart inputs.

event.summary: Deleting the tmux branch matches the narrowed release-test contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 6f1a36144ede6f87c33c0bfedd871c208cc930d4. TLDR: considered whether deleting the old-session-in-tmux tests silently removes promised release-gate coverage. The same revision explicitly narrows this test to previous releases with a terminal host. Details: the removed tmux and previous_can_create_hosts test cases are replaced by test_guest_operations.py:939-977, which refuses both a new no-host baseline and a retained older no-host receipt. test_guest_workflow.py removes the source-layout cross-check because this path no longer infers terminal support from crate layout. BRICK-TEST.md:420-422 says "Its terminal sample is refused until that attempt has observed the captured session, and requires exactly one terminal host with one live child: a previous stable that runs the session anywhere else cannot be tested this way." BRICK-TEST.md:440-441 says "This test does not check that the upgrade ends the old terminals releases before terminal hosts left running; the supervisor’s Rust tests cover that startup step." Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source and explicit test contract; no execution. proposed_drop: the removed path is explicitly excluded from the revised release-test contract and the replacement fails closed rather than accepting a tmux fixture. Could-be-highest: no established highest consequence; maintainer test coverage only, with no demonstrated catastrophic outcome. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this review does not verify the separate supervisor Rust tests or judge the product’s tmux-retirement behavior, which are outside the assigned patches.

event.summary: The remote new-session lifetime remains required after sampling is removed
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 6f1a36144ede6f87c33c0bfedd871c208cc930d4. TLDR: considered whether the relaxed new-session instructions remove the running remote session needed to judge host Remove and Uninstall. They do not. Details: test_guest_workflow.py:123-138 tests both managed and plain envelopes and requires the keep-running text exactly for the remote checkpoint. guest_workflow.py:341-343 and :452-454 retain that instruction, while local instructions :327-334 and :438-443 leave the old session untouched. BRICK-TEST.md:413-414 says "The remote check’s new session must keep running: the Remove and Uninstall checks carry it." Local old-session survival now samples its own hosts and does not require the unrelated new local session (guest_operations.py:699-729). Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source and delivered instruction assertions; no execution. proposed_drop: the remote lifetime premise remains in both envelopes and is directly asserted; dropping the local keep-running requirement is compatible with the independent survival sample. Could-be-highest: no; this is maintainer test-premise coverage, without an established security or loss-of-work route. possible_cover: none. Caveat: these tests establish instruction delivery, not that a live model follows the instruction; the tests accurately state that limit in their class documentation.

event.summary: Discarding the second remote host return value preserves fixture cleanup ownership
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 6f1a36144ede6f87c33c0bfedd871c208cc930d4. TLDR: checked whether changing the second remote stand-in launch to an unassigned call loses ownership of a live process or its pipes. Source refutes that concern. Details: test_guest_operations.py:1104-1106 creates the Popen and immediately registers self.stop_host with that exact object in addCleanup before returning it. The changed :1159 call therefore still retains the process object for cleanup even though the test body no longer names it. stop_host at :1111-1117 closes its stdin, waits with a ten-second bound and closes stdout; the child-owning script at :1096-1103 closes child stdin and waits when host stdin ends. Cleanup registration precedes readiness failure paths at :1107-1109. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed source-level ownership analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: cleanup ownership lives in the registered unittest cleanup, not the removed local variable, so this edit does not establish a leak. Could-be-highest: no; owned maintainer fixture resources only, without an established catastrophic consequence. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this does not certify unrelated pre-existing fixture failure handling, and no runtime teardown behavior was observed. Rejected discovery-pass candidate.
